title: T3 Android GLES3 color / alpha / sRGB device checks

tests.title: Driver and baseline RGB
tests.instructions: Launch on the POCO F5 Pro. Select CASE01 and verify distinct red, green, blue columns. Record screenshot and export logs; no Raft game assets are used.
tests.expected: Three opaque RGB columns and GLES_VENDOR/RENDERER/VERSION in exported JSONL.

tests.title: Vertex colors
tests.instructions: Select CASE02; inspect four corners and gradient center. Record whether any area is unexpectedly solid white.
tests.expected: A smooth four-corner vertex-color gradient, not a uniformly white card.

tests.title: Straight alpha smoke
tests.instructions: Select CASE03; examine red smoke-like translucent overlay against blue background. Capture the area and compare with square smoke in Raft screenshot as a qualitative reference only.
tests.expected: Blue background remains visible beneath red layer; no unintended opaque rectangular particle.

tests.title: Premultiplied alpha contract
tests.instructions: Select CASE04; compare left straight-alpha panel with right premultiplied-alpha panel, both over blue. Note any obvious brightness discrepancy.
tests.expected: Panels look approximately equal when GL blend factors match the supplied alpha encoding.

tests.title: Texture sRGB decode
tests.instructions: Select CASE05; compare equal 128-encoded gray textures sampled with UNORM on left and sRGB on right.
tests.expected: sRGB half on right is visibly darker; recorded left/right pixels differ. This is not Unity color-space validation.

tests.title: GLSL compile negative control
tests.instructions: Select CASE06; export logs and find negative_control; verify deliberately malformed shader failed to compile while a valid blue background still displays.
tests.expected: negative_control PASS invalid shader rejected; fallback draws and no unexpected GL error.
